leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - 2010 ruling on pride parade bans
leads.documents: Systemic refusal by Russian city authorities to authorize pride parades; discrimination against gay community; establishes enforcement pattern applicable in Kabardino-Balkaria as federal precedent.
leads.detail: Cited in text as: 'In 2010, Russia was fined by the European Court of Human Rights' per Alexeyev claims about Moscow Pride. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: Federal law on propaganda of non-traditional sexual relationships (2013)
leads.documents: Criminalizes distribution of 'propaganda' promoting 'non-traditional sexual relationships' among minors; basis for censorship, arrests, and rise in hate crimes nationwide including Kabardino-Balkaria.
leads.detail: Cited as 2013 federal law passed by Russian Duma unanimously. No URL visible in provided text.

leads.title: United Nations Human Rights Council expert panel report - 13 April 2017
leads.documents: Wave of torture and killings of gay men in Chechnya (North Caucasus region neighboring Kabardino-Balkaria); documents extrajudicial detention/torture machinery.
leads.detail: Cited as 'report issued on 13 April 2017, a panel of five expert advisors to the United Nations Human Rights Council'. No URL visible.

leads.title: 2022 expansion of propaganda law
leads.documents: Expands propaganda ban to anyone regardless of age and prohibits materials making minors interested in gender transition; directly affects transgender expression/visibility in Kabardino-Balkaria.
leads.detail: Cited as 2022 expansion amid Russo-Ukrainian war. No URL visible.

leads.title: Federal law banning gender transition - July 2023
leads.documents: Prohibits both gender-affirming surgery and legal gender recognition outright; bans legal gender change; core trans legal-status law applicable in Kabardino-Balkaria.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In July 2023, Russia enacted a law banning gender transition' and 1 July 2023 new laws. No URL visible.

leads.title: Federal adoption ban law - 2024
leads.documents: Bans adoption of Russian children by citizens/residents of countries that allow gender transitions; part of anti-trans family-rights machinery.
leads.detail: Cited as 'in 2024 passed a law banning the adoption of Russian children'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Supreme Court of Russia ruling - November 2023 designating 'international LGBT public movement' as extremist
leads.documents: Criminalizes LGBT activism/participation, financing, and display of symbols like rainbow flag; added 22 March 2024 to 'unified list of terrorist and extremist organizations and persons'; enforcement basis for arrests of club owners and flag displays.
leads.detail: Cited as November 2023 Supreme Court ruling following Ministry of Justice lawsuit; formal listing 22 March 2024 as 'Международное общественное движение ЛГБТ и его структурные подразделения'. No URL visible.

leads.title: European Court of Human Rights - Fedotova and Others v. Russia (2021)
leads.documents: Rules failure to offer any legal recognition to same-sex relationships violates human rights; documents lack of same-sex union recognition; notes Russia left court in 2022.
leads.detail: Cited as '2021 case Fedotova and Others v. Russia'. No URL visible.

leads.title: Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) report - December 2018
leads.documents: Confirms claims that persecution of LGBTQ persons in Chechnya took place and was ignored by authorities; institutional verification of North Caucasus anti-LGBTQ purge.
leads.detail: Cited as 'report released in December 2018 by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE)'. No URL visible.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Rainbow ranking reports - 2016, 2019, 2024
leads.documents: Ranks Russia 2nd least LGBTQ-friendly in Europe (2016), 46th of 49 (2019), worst of 49 surveyed (2024); documents country-level rights climate applicable to Kabardino-Balkaria.
leads.detail: Cited as ILGA-Europe placements in text. No URL visible.
